notes: Difficult shared cases for the investigation cluster. The discriminations: root-cause diagnosis (systematic-debugging) vs descriptive orientation (codebase-orientation) vs finding-level security review of a change (security-review) vs structured threat modeling (threat-modeling). Cross-cutting cases that expect architecture-review or implementation-planning appear in the review-family and design-change-family sets where those skills are candidate options.

cases.prompt: The authorization test fails intermittently in CI but not locally. I want the failure explained before we discuss whether the design is secure.
cases.notes: Security vocabulary (authorization) but the dominant job is root-cause diagnosis, explicitly fenced off from a security review.

cases.prompt: I just joined the team. Can you onboard me to the acme-web repo - explain what it does and how it's structured, and where the payment retry path lives?
cases.notes: No diagnosis, no review, no threat model: a descriptive evidence-backed map is the deliverable.

cases.prompt: Our agent workflow ingests untrusted web pages and then runs tools. Build the threat model: trust boundaries, attacker profiles, prioritized abuse paths, and mitigations tied to components.
cases.notes: A structured model of the system's boundaries is the deliverable, not a review of a specific change and not a diagnosis.

cases.prompt: Review this authentication endpoint for a likely SQL-injection vulnerability and safely test it against our local build.
cases.notes: A finding-level review with local verification is the deliverable; threat-modeling is the tempting neighbor.

cases.prompt: The search endpoint returns a 500 on certain inputs. Find the root cause.
We know the search endpoint 500s because of an unvalidated range parameter. Map the request path and the code that handles it so the new engineer can make the fix.
cases.notes: Pair B: cause known; the deliverable is a descriptive map of the relevant path, not a diagnosis.

cases.prompt: Our search endpoint returns a 500 error on certain inputs. Is this a security problem or just a bug?
cases.notes: Deliberately underdetermined: it could be a bug (debugging), a security issue (security-review), or something structural (threat-modeling). Clarification or a documented tie-breaker is required.

cases.prompt: The function crashes with a null value. Trace where the invariant was violated instead of adding a guard at the crash site.
cases.notes: Explicit anti-bandage instruction: root-cause tracing is the job.

cases.prompt: The new multi-tenant API has a session token that's readable by any tenant and I also want to understand the overall architecture. First priority: tell me whether the token issue is exploitable.
cases.notes: Two intents; the stated first priority is a finding-level security verdict on a concrete defect.

cases.prompt: Our agent workflow fetches web pages and feeds them into an LLM that can call tools. Review the workflow code for indirect prompt injection and sensitive-context leakage.
cases.notes: Pair A: finding-level review of the existing workflow implementation.

cases.prompt: We are designing a NEW agent workflow that will ingest untrusted web pages and run tools. Build the threat model before any code is written: trust boundaries, STRIDE abuse paths, mitigations.
cases.notes: Pair B: forward-looking modeling before implementation. Same domain, different deliverable.

cases.prompt: Map the repository at ./billing-service so I can find where payment retries are handled.
cases.notes: The deliverable is a map, not a diagnosis of the retry behavior.

cases.prompt: The upload job fails about 1 in 10 CI runs with a connection-reset error.

turns.user: The upload job fails about 1 in 10 CI runs with a connection-reset error. Diagnose why - and don't just slap a retry loop on it.
Good, the cause is the proxy dropping idle connections. Now harden the job so it survives those resets, with a regression test first.

cases.notes: Diagnosis first, then hardening: ownership must transition between turns.

cases.prompt: We just built a new multi-tenant API. Should we worry about security?
cases.notes: Too little evidence to route: could be threat-modeling (design-time), security-review (implementation), or requirements. Clarification is required.
